title: Sephiria Co-op Guide — 4-Player Runs, Trading & Revives (1.0)
description: Sephiria co-op guide: how four-player runs change enemy pressure, what to trade, how revives work, and which builds carry a party.
meta: Covers sephiria co-op / coop / four-player run searches; lobby setup lives on the multiplayer page.
body:
Co-op in Sephiria is online Steam co-op for up to four players, and it changes how a run plays: enemy pressure scales with the party, and the group can trade items and revive each other. For lobby setup, start with the multiplayer setup page — this page is about actually playing together.

What changes in co-op

SystemSingle playerIn co-op
Party sizeOneUp to four players, joined through Steam invites
EnemiesBaseline density and healthReported to scale with the number of players
ItemsYours onlyYou can trade items with the party
DeathRun overA teammate can revive you mid-run
Loot pressureEverything is yoursArtifact and Tablet competition is real — agree grid priorities before the run

Co-op builds that pull their weight

  • Companion / summoner — summons soak aggro, which is worth more in a party than solo. See the companion build.
  • Freeze control (Dagger route) — locking down normal enemies lets the damage player work. See builds.
  • Tank sword and shield — block and reflect builds are the natural revive-buddy role.
  • Ranged crossbow — safe damage while melee players hold the line.

Practical co-op habits

  • Agree the grid split before floor one. Tablets and Artifacts are shared loot, so decide who spends Tablets on what.
  • Trade duplicates instead of vendoring them. Item trading is built in, so a drop you cannot use may complete a teammate's route.
  • Keep one player on revive duty. Revives are the single biggest co-op advantage — a party that ignores them plays harder than solo.
  • Match difficulty to the weakest member. Enemy scaling makes a carried player a liability, and Hard Mode is a per-run choice.
  • Expect host-authoritative progress. The session belongs to the host, so a host disconnect is the usual cause of a broken lobby.

If co-op will not start

  • Both host and guest should finish the prologue and tutorial before trying to join.
  • Look for the village co-op access point after the tutorial rather than expecting an option on the title screen.
  • Confirm the invite actually reached your friend through Steam — the lobby uses Steam invites, not in-game lobby codes.
The four-player limit, item trading and revives are from the Steam listing; the monster-scaling behaviour is reported by a third-party review rather than stated officially, so treat it as a community observation.
